analysis.title: The Hottest Trade On Wall Street Gets A Field Manual: Barclays Maps The AI CDS Market, And How To Trade It
key_insights: Barclays' credit strategy team (Jigar Patel) published 'A roadmap for AI CDS', covering ten AI-related issuers in CDX IG Series 47: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, SpaceX, AMD, Broadcom, Intel and Nvidia. All ten have widened over six months and trade toward the wide end of their six-month ranges.

The spread gap between the AI cohort and CDX IG went from roughly 10bp six months ago to 76bp now, 5bp inside the record 81bp set October 23. 31bp of the widening came after the September 21 index roll.
The ten AI issuers are 8% of CDX IG constituents but 16% (about 10bp) of the index's intrinsic spread.

Chipmakers Broadcom, AMD and Nvidia were among the tightest names six months ago (low 40bp area) and are now among the widest. 5Y CDS is up 258% for Broadcom, 177% for AMD and 172% for Nvidia over six months, versus +20% for Microsoft, the cohort's lone AAA.
Barclays calls Broadcom, AMD and Nvidia the 'chip-financing names' because vendor financing, guarantees and SPVs make the credit market price them like lenders with concentrated loan books.

The CDS-cash basis (CDS spread minus maturity-matched bond spread) for AI names has risen about 50bp over a year and is now positive, while the non-AI basis is little changed. Protection on AI names costs more than the extra bond yield, which indicates protection demand from investors who do not own the bonds.
The chip-financing trio and Oracle have the most positive bases. Intel is the only name still negative (-14bp).

Rolling four-week average weekly CDS volume as of October 23 was about $6B for the six hyperscalers and $3B for the four chipmakers, up roughly 740% and 1,900% year over year, partly from low starting points.
The AI cohort was under 5% of Americas corporate single-name CDS volume a year ago, as much as 36% in August and about 20% now.
Year to date, CDS trading tied to the 10 largest hyperscalers and chipmakers rose more than eightfold to $176B, with Oracle alone at $46.8B, up nearly sixfold.

Net notional outstanding on hyperscalers is about $20B (from about $5B) and on chipmakers $8.6B (from about $1.9B), over $28B in total versus about $7B a year ago. The ten names are nearly 14% of Americas corporate single-name CDS open interest, up from 4%.
Oracle ranks first among 340 Americas corporate single-name CDS in both volume and open interest. Its CDS went from 75bp last November to 300bp this month.

Amazon and Alphabet both trade near 80-81bp in 5Y CDS, but Amazon's 3s5s curve is only 18bp and has steepened just 2bp in six months. Barclays attributes this to technical buying pressure from the June delayed-draw term loan.

Amazon reported Q3 free cash flow of -$33.5B versus a $7.7B consensus, capex of $77.3B and $48B of new debt raised in the quarter. The stock was down 7.3% premarket Friday and no 2027 capex number was given.

Intel's 3s5s curve is steep for its spread level, and it is the only name at 100% of its six-month range. Intel stock fell as much as 29.7% on Friday after weak Q4 guidance and a warning of no positive cash flow this year.
ICE clearing data show 85-90% of cleared risk for MSFT, GOOGL, META, NVDA and SPCX sits in the 4-5Y area. Amazon's largest cleared bucket is June 2029 and Intel's is December 2029.

CoreWeave is the only directly AI-related contract in CDX.HY. Its 5Y CDS trades at 15.5 points upfront versus a six-month range of -2.3 to 20 points. Four-week average weekly volume is $302M (from $32M) and net notional is $850M (from $65M).

Supply is continuing: Microsoft launched a $25B-plus 10-part bond deal (first since 2017), Amazon disclosed $48B of new debt in a quarter, and Broadcom may sell up to about $21B of bonds early next year to fund the Anthropic chip deal.

market_movers.rationale: Barclays recommends buying AVGO 5Y CDS protection to hedge the broader AI funding overhang. Broadcom CDS hit a record closing high of 175.4bp on Thursday per ICE, versus 168bp in the Barclays tables.
Barclays credit analysts are Underweight. Free cash flow of -$33.5B in Q3 and $48B of new debt contrast with a flat 3s5s CDS curve.
Barclays suggests selling the ORCL 5Y basis because the basis is among the most positive in the cohort and CDS lagged the cash rally after Oracle capped capital raises at $20B over FY27-FY30.
Barclays high yield analysts remain Overweight CoreWeave. Its 9.75% 2031 bonds were quoted at 82.5 on Tuesday and its 5Y CDS is at 15.5 points upfront.
Intel is in the cohort 'for completeness' and has not taken part in vendor financing. Its steep curve and negative basis may not survive after Friday's stock decline.

sector_views.rationale: Spreads have widened sharply, CDS underperforms both the index and cash bonds, and heavy bond supply continues. This is the view of the article's author, not Barclays' formal sector stance.

earnings_insights: Amazon Q3 (reported Thursday after Barclays' note): free cash flow reported at -$33.5B versus $7.7B consensus, capex $77.3B, and $48B of new long-term debt raised in the quarter. No 2027 capex figure was given.
Intel Q4 guidance (given Thursday) came in well below consensus. The company warned it does not expect positive cash flow this year. The stock fell as much as 29.7% Friday.
Oracle (October 28) said it would cap additional capital raises at $20B over FY27-FY30. Oracle CDS fell the most in nearly nine months that day.
Alphabet's CDS rose 5bp to about 84bp Thursday after what the article calls Alphabet's worst stock day ever.

trade_ideas.rationale: Hedge the broader AI funding overhang, including Broadcom's guarantee of the Anthropic chip deal and potential bond issuance of about $21B.

trade_ideas.description: Buy AMZN 5Y CDS protection outright, or a DV01-neutral 3s5s steepener (sell 3Y protection, buy 5Y)
trade_ideas.rationale: Amazon's 3s5s curve is flat relative to Alphabet's at the same 5Y level, and Barclays expects normalization after the term loan's technical effect on the 2.5-3.0y points.

trade_ideas.description: Sell the ORCL 5Y basis: sell the 5.25% 2032 bonds and sell 5Y or 5.5Y protection
trade_ideas.rationale: Oracle's basis is among the most positive in the cohort and CDS lagged the cash rally on October 28, so Barclays expects compression.

risk_factors: Heavy continuing bond, SPV, lease-guarantee and vendor-loan supply from AI borrowers.
Deteriorating free cash flow and rising capex guidance (Amazon, Intel, Oracle).
Vendor financing concentrates loan-book-like credit risk in chipmakers.
Gartner predicts over 80% of neoclouds will fold (cited for CoreWeave).
CDS volume is volatile and part of the growth reflects low starting points.
charts_described: Barclays shows the spread gap between AI-related issuers and CDX IG widening from roughly 10bp to 76bp over six months, with 31bp after the September 21 roll.
Barclays' scorecard shows Intel at 100% of its six-month range.
Barclays' basis chart shows the AI cohort's CDS-cash basis rising about 50bp to positive over a year, while non-AI is little changed.
vol_and_positioning: Barclays shows the AI cohort at 16% of CDX IG intrinsic spread against 8% of constituents. Goldman's Alisha Pasi is cited saying the index is becoming a less precise expression of the risk investors own, which pushes investors toward single names.

Protection demand comes from equity funds hedging AI portfolios, banks hedging counterparty and construction-loan exposure, and macro participants. Goldman said in August that synthetic CDS volumes traded 20x reference obligations.
AI names are nearly 14% of Americas single-name CDS open interest, and six of the ten rank among the ten most actively traded Americas corporate CDS contracts.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's Alisha Pasi: the index is becoming a less precise expression of the risk investors own.
Goldman's sales and trading desk told clients in August that synthetic CDS volumes were trading 20x reference obligations.
Goldman reported record 'tourist' demand for CRWV debt and Oracle CDS (cited October 19).
Barclays' high yield analysts remain Overweight CoreWeave while the article notes the CDS pricing sends a different signal.

tension_points.bull_case: A deeper, more liquid CDS market signals a maturing asset class. Meta's $95B equity raise and Oracle's $20B capital-raise cap show hyperscalers getting more disciplined on funding.
tension_points.bear_case: Equity raises happen when the debt window gets expensive. Microsoft, an AAA issuer, tapped the market for $25B the morning after its CFO said it had not 'yet' tapped debt. Amazon raised $48B of debt in one quarter and Broadcom may issue about $21B.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A visible drop in AI-related bond and SPV issuance, with improving free cash flow and capex guidance, would undercut the bear case.
